races.name: Family Fun Day 'National Hunt' Maiden Hurdle (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Saint Jeannais
runners_data.note: Front-runner returning after 176 days off but has course-and-distance winning form and handles good ground well

runners_data.name: Mr Mojo Risin
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with solid recent Kelso fourth who should appreciate the strong early pace from his tracking position
runners_data.comment: Displayed clear promise on both hurdle starts last season and has big role to play here
runners_data.spotlight: Displayed clear promise on both hurdling starts last season, more recently when fourth at Kelso (2m, good to soft) six weeks ago, and ought to play a significant role here; tongue-tie fitted for first time.

runners_data.name: Maskarvel
runners_data.note: Another front-runner with decent recent Huntingdon second but may struggle if forced into speed duel with Saint Jeannais
runners_data.comment: Ran well to be second in a Huntingdon maiden, for all that only three got round
runners_data.spotlight: Promise in Irish bumpers and ran well to be second in a Huntingdon maiden, for all that only three got round; looks mildly progressive.

runners_data.name: Anxious Moments
runners_data.note: Prominent type who struggled badly on recent starts and needs major improvement despite 7lb weight allowance
runners_data.comment: Struggled over C&D on rules debut and dropped out of contention tamely on next outing
runners_data.spotlight: Struggled over C&D on last month's rules debut and dropped out of contention very tamely at Uttoxeter (2m, good) a fortnight ago; huge improvement required.

runners_data.name: Lilycala
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with 7lb claiming rider whose only run saw saddle slip, making assessment difficult
runners_data.comment: Always behind when 200-1 for good-ground Stratford bumper last month
runners_data.spotlight: Always behind (albeit saddle slipped) when 200-1 for good-ground Stratford bumper last month.

runners_data.name: Noble Don
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who has been well beaten in two hurdle attempts at longer trips
runners_data.comment: Well beaten at triple-digit odds in first two hurdle races
runners_data.spotlight: Well beaten at triple-digit odds in first two hurdle races (2m5f/2m); can't be recommended.

runners_data.name: Heffalump
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning from 167-day break after wind operation, related to Grand National winner Ballabriggs
runners_data.comment: Struggled in soft-ground bumper in November; given wind op in December; hurdle debut
runners_data.spotlight: Out of a sister to stable's Grand National winner Ballabriggs but struggled in a soft-ground bumper in November and needs subsequent wind op to have made a big difference.

runners_data.name: Masterfield
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with 7lb allowance who fell last time after modest hurdle debut
runners_data.comment: Well held when third of four on hurdle debut in March and fell mid-race on next outing
runners_data.spotlight: Well held when third of four on hurdle debut in March and fell mid-race on next outing; probably one for further down the line.

runners_data.name: Knolton Park
runners_data.note: Hold-up type making stable debut for Venetia Williams after 295 days off and uninspiring bumper form
runners_data.comment: Showed only minor promise in three bumpers in early part of last season; now with new yard
runners_data.spotlight: Showed nothing more than minor promise in three bumpers for David Loughnane in early part of last season and needs to take a big step forward on this stable/hurdle debut.

runners_data.name: Cappa Lass
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner with first-time headgear who was soundly beaten in two recent hurdle starts
runners_data.comment: Second in a Irish point last year but soundly beaten in first two hurdle races
runners_data.spotlight: Came second in an Irish point last spring but, following a layoff, was soundly beaten in two hurdle races last month (1m7f/2m)

runners_data.name: Magna Patch
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who showed minor promise on debut but fades late and may struggle with strong early pace
runners_data.comment: Has shown some ability but will probably be of greater interest when switched to handicaps
runners_data.spotlight: Displayed minor promise on hurdle debut at Ludlow (2m, good to soft) in February and may not have been suited by soft ground when well beaten last month but will probably be of greater interest when switched to handicaps.

runners_data.name: Pretty Darn Quick
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who was tailed off on hurdling debut 14 days ago and appears outclassed
runners_data.comment: In rear throughout when 250-1 for hurdling debut at Uttoxeter a fortnight ago
runners_data.spotlight: In rear throughout when 250-1 for hurdling debut at Uttoxeter a fortnight ago.

runners_data.name: Dinkys Rose
runners_data.note: Prominent type with 7lb allowance but has shown no significant promise in four previous starts
runners_data.comment: Yet to show any significant promise after contesting a bumper and three maiden hurdles
runners_data.spotlight: Yet to show any significant promise after contesting a bumper and three maiden hurdles (all 2m).

races.paceDynamic: Saint Jeannais and Maskarvel will contest the early lead, with both confirmed front-runners likely to set an honest gallop over this trip. Mr Mojo Risin will track prominently behind the leaders, while the large contingent of hold-up horses including Heffalump, Knolton Park, Lilycala and Cappa Lass will settle at the rear. With two keen pace-setters up front and a 13-runner field, the tempo should be solid rather than stop-start, creating a searching test over the final half-mile. This race shape strongly favours prominent racers and patient hold-up horses who can pick up the pieces when the pace-setters weaken, while making life difficult for those needing to be handy throughout.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Late
scenarios.trigger: If Saint Jeannais and Maskarvel go too hard early and fold in the final furlong
scenarios.body: The honest gallop will find out the leaders' stamina reserves, allowing the best of the hold-up horses to sweep through late. Patient tactics and class will prevail over early positioning.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Mr Mojo Risin can sit perfectly behind the pace-setters and time his challenge
scenarios.body: The prominent position gives him first run on the leaders when they weaken, avoiding the traffic problems that could beset the hold-up brigade. His recent Kelso form suggests he has the tactical speed to capitalize.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Saint Jeannais or Maskarvel gets an uncontested lead and controls the tempo
scenarios.body: One pace-setter could steal a march by dictating fractions, building an unassailable advantage while the hold-up horses leave too much to do. Saint Jeannais's course-and-distance win gives him the edge in this scenario.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Maiden Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If the market leaders all disappoint and a lesser-fancied runner finds improvement
scenarios.body: The competitive nature of maidens can produce shock results when established runners fail to progress. A horse showing hurdling aptitude for the first time could capitalize on others' shortcomings.

watchPoints.text: Saint Jeannais and Maskarvel could set unsustainable fractions if both insist on leading, compromising each other's chances
Several hold-up horses including Heffalump and Knolton Park are returning from long layoffs which may blunt their finishing kicks
Mr Mojo Risin's prominent racing style could prove ideal if he can avoid getting involved in the early pace battle
Multiple runners with recent poor form including Anxious Moments and Pretty Darn Quick look outclassed at current levels
The 7lb claiming riders on Lilycala, Masterfield and Dinkys Rose add an element of unpredictability to their chances

races.name: Wigan Beer Company Novices' Limited Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Greer Hill
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer with jumping issues, 46 days off and weak recent form makes him vulnerable despite style suiting
runners_data.comment: Weakened quickly on March's handicap debut (2m1f); hopes rest with the debuted tongue-tie.
runners_data.spotlight: Jumping issues less evident than before, but still didn't lay down any sort of marker on March's handicap debut after five months out (2m1f, good to soft), weakening quickly; hopes rest with the debuted tongue-tie.

runners_data.name: Dante's Inferno
runners_data.note: Classic hold-up horse returning to optimal 2m3f trip after 223-day break, form suggests this distance suits better
runners_data.comment: Lacks recent match practice, but another go at today's sort of trip looks the way to go.
runners_data.spotlight: Enough in his final two races last year (one here) suggested a return to 2m3f-2m4f is worth a go, having paid for trying to take on the winner on his previous run at such a trip; longest absent in the line-up.

runners_data.name: Mr Mahler
runners_data.note: Prominent runner but 0-15 record and declining form over fences suggests he's past his best despite new tactics
runners_data.comment: Not at his best over fences when last seen; 8lb lower than for most recent hurdles run.
runners_data.spotlight: Decline in fortunes over fences last season wasn't arrested by a switch to front-running; brave to name this the day given he's 0-15 now, but new career-low mark is notably 8lb lower than when last trying hurdles.

runners_data.name: Dream's Ka
runners_data.note: Strong hold-up horse just 12 days since encouraging Fakenham second, Skelton team in good form and trip suits perfectly
runners_data.comment: 2l second at Fakenham latest (2m4f, good); player if he can settle better this time.
runners_data.spotlight: The strength of this month's 2l Fakenham second (2m4f, good) hasn't been tested yet, but he's undeniably starting to find his level in handicaps; back up 2lb and could ideally race more sparingly than on that occasion, but among the likeliest all the same.

runners_data.name: My Fortune
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who needs to improve significantly, 53 days off and wind surgery may help but handicap career stalled
runners_data.comment: Only minor revival in tongue-tie latest; chances rest on response to wind surgery.
runners_data.spotlight: Handicap career yet to take off, only reviving a little for the debuted tongue-tie at Southwell latest (2m5f, good); positive response to wind surgery likelier more significant to his chances here than a 3lb ease.

runners_data.name: Siege Of Acres
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer struggling over fences lately, needs to show more stamina at this longer trip
runners_data.comment: Returns to hurdling on a more realistic mark, but needs to tease out resources longer.
runners_data.spotlight: Early switch to chasing hasn't gone entirely to plan; looking a bit more realistic now, but needs to tease out his resources longer.

runners_data.name: Asta La Vista
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who refused to settle last time and lost shoe, step back up in trip should help settling
runners_data.comment: Excuses on recent handicap debut (2m); player dropped 2lb and stepped back up in trip.
runners_data.spotlight: Likely capable of better in handicaps than he could show at Ffos Las latest (2m, good), having refused to settle and then lost a shoe; step back up in trip appeals on pedigree, and 2lb drop is a nice bonus.

runners_data.name: Peace In The Park
runners_data.note: Reliable hold-up horse with respectable handicap record, recent Taunton third over similar trip looks solid form
runners_data.comment: Fair work late on at Taunton latest (2m3f, good); likelier to run his race than many.
runners_data.spotlight: Basically respectable efforts on most handicap outings so far (a lost shoe excused the one flop), doing fair late work for last month's Taunton third (2m3f, good); likelier to give his running than many.

runners_data.name: Vinnie O'Neil
runners_data.note: Hold-up type but finished 50 lengths last at this course and distance 28 days ago, 5lb drop insufficient
runners_data.comment: Faded into a 50l last of seven on recent return (C&D); down 5lb but unpersuasive.
runners_data.spotlight: Yet to finish off a race especially strongly, including when a 50l last of seven on last month's C&D return (good); latest 5lb drop isn't sufficiently persuasive.

runners_data.name: Vesalius
runners_data.note: Prominent runner returning after 210 days off, beaten 58 lengths when last seen and no chances taken with mark
runners_data.comment: 58l third on most recent start in the autumn (2m6f, good); initial mark not a gift.
runners_data.spotlight: Beaten 58l when placing at Stratford last October (2m6f, good), and unseen since; no chances taken with his initial mark.

runners_data.name: Nevershedatear
runners_data.note: Only front-runner who will get uncontested lead, 6lb rise for C&D second looks steep but style advantage significant
runners_data.comment: C&D mares' handicap second in March (good) off 6lb lower; potential pace rivalry awaits.
runners_data.spotlight: Enters the reckoning on March's C&D mares' handicap second (good; beaten just over 1l), and race came too soon next time; 6lb rise appears steep, however, and there's potential rivalry for the lead here.

races.paceDynamic: Nevershedatear is the sole confirmed front-runner and will get an uncontested lead from the start. The prominent runners Mr Mahler, Asta La Vista and Vesalius lack the early pace to pressure him, creating a sustainable rhythm through the early stages. This moderate gallop will set up perfectly for the strong contingent of hold-up horses including Dream's Ka, Dante's Inferno, Greer Hill, My Fortune, Siege Of Acres, Peace In The Park and Vinnie O'Neil to unleash finishing kicks. The lack of early pressure on Nevershedatear combined with the 2m3½f trip strongly favours hold-up horses who can produce late surges.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Nevershedatear sets uncontested fractions and the pace stays moderate throughout
scenarios.body: The lack of early speed allows patient hold-up horses to get into perfect striking positions turning for home. Dream's Ka, Dante's Inferno and Peace In The Park can all unleash telling late runs to sweep past a weakening leader.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Nevershedatear kicks clear approaching the final flight and none of the hold-up horses can respond
scenarios.body: His recent C&D second suggests he has the stamina for this trip when allowed easy fractions. The hold-up horses fail to close quickly enough on the testing ground, leaving Nevershedatear clear.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Mr Mahler or Asta La Vista track closer than usual and kick approaching two out
scenarios.body: One of the prominent runners gets first run on the field while Nevershedatear weakens and before the hold-up horses can respond. This tactical switch catches the field flat-footed in the closing stages.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Benefits Outsider
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses completely or there are multiple jumping errors at crucial stages
scenarios.body: The race falls apart tactically, allowing an unconsidered runner like Vesalius or Siege Of Acres to benefit from the mayhem. Normal form lines go out the window in a muddling contest.

watchPoints.text: Nevershedatear could get such an easy lead that none of the hold-up horses can peg him back despite the style mismatch
Dream's Ka only had 12 days between runs and quick turnaround might blunt his finishing kick when it matters most
Mr Mahler's front-running tactics could put unexpected pressure on Nevershedatear if he tracks closer than usual early
The ground could be more testing than advertised given the consistent 'Good' readings across all six races on the card
Asta La Vista's settling issues last time might resurface if the pace is too slow and he gets lit up early again

races.name: Remembering Kitty Warburton Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Fasol
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with strong Nicholls form who should relish the expected strong gallop but needs clear passage late
runners_data.comment: Gave it a good shot from the front when third in competitive Sandown handicap last month
runners_data.spotlight: Largely consistent 7yo who gave it a good shot from the front when third in competitive Sandown handicap (2m4f, good) last month; eased in grade here and will be fine over the shorter trip; major contender.

runners_data.name: Fromheretoeternity
runners_data.note: Consistent closer whose 27-day break is ideal and brings solid recent form to this easier grade

runners_data.name: Diamonds Galore
runners_data.note: Prominent runner perfectly placed to track Krak and avoid the traffic problems facing hold-up horses

runners_data.name: Dog Fox
runners_data.note: Long-absent hold-up horse returning to hurdles at ideal course and distance, just 1lb above last winning mark
runners_data.comment: Failed to complete two of three chases in the autumn; reverts to hurdling after a break
runners_data.spotlight: Failed to complete two of his three chases in the autumn and now reverts to hurdling after a break; suited by this C&D and only 1lb above his last winning mark but entitled to benefit from this outing.

runners_data.name: Krak
runners_data.note: The lone front runner sporting first-time cheekpieces who should get uncontested lead but questionable stamina reserves
runners_data.comment: Had disappointing campaign for new stable last season; tried in cheekpieces here
runners_data.spotlight: Made winning handicap debut in Ireland in April 2025 but had disappointing campaign for new stable last season; drops back in trip and sports first-time cheekpieces here; needs to turn a corner.

runners_data.name: Roysse
runners_data.note: Failed chaser reverting to hurdles with hold-up style that needs strong pace to be effective late
runners_data.comment: Chasing didn't go to plan last season and he was well beaten when back over hurdles
runners_data.spotlight: Chasing didn't go to plan last season (four attempts) and he was easily reeled in after making the running on return to hurdling in March; on a tempting mark now but his tendency to race far too freely remains a worry, and others are much less risky.

runners_data.name: City Of Diamonds
runners_data.note: Prominent type whose recent soft ground form raises questions about effectiveness on good surface

runners_data.name: Itsinthename
runners_data.note: Unexposed 5-year-old hold-up horse whose limited hurdle experience could mask significant improvement potential
runners_data.comment: Maiden winner; had excuse last time (bled); makes handicap debut; still has potential
runners_data.spotlight: Unexposed 5yo who won Catterick maiden (1m7f, good to soft) on stable/hurdle debut in February; not discredited in good race on next outing and had excuse for heavy defeat last time (bled from the nose); makes handicap debut here; could still have potential.

runners_data.name: Paddockwood
runners_data.note: Ex-French hold-up horse with concerning finishing tendencies who has struggled in British handicap company
runners_data.comment: Down the field on first two British starts but given wind op since; improvement possible
runners_data.spotlight: Ex-French 4yo who finished down the field on first two British starts, in juvenile handicaps at Cheltenham Festival and Ascot in March; not beaten far on latter occasion, though, and had wind surgery soon afterwards; may yet come good for Ben Pauling.

races.paceDynamic: Krak is the only confirmed front runner in this field and should get an uncontested lead, setting a sustainable gallop throughout the 2m½f trip. The prominent runners Diamonds Galore and City Of Diamonds will track close enough but are unlikely to pressure the leader early. With six hold-up horses including Fasol, Fromheretoeternity, and Dog Fox needing room to maneuver late, this becomes a tactical puzzle where the leader may steal too much ground. This race shape clearly favors either the uncontested front runner or the most talented hold-up horse who can produce the best late kick.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Krak Wires Field
scenarios.trigger: If Krak gets easy early fractions and maintains his stamina edge
scenarios.body: The leader builds an insurmountable advantage turning for home while the hold-up brigade leaves their challenges too late. Krak's drop in trip and first-time cheekpieces could provide the extra edge needed to hold off late challengers.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes truly pedestrian and allows a strong finishing kick
scenarios.body: The crawling gallop plays into the hands of the classiest closer who can unleash a devastating turn of foot. Fasol's Nicholls training and consistent form gives him the edge in a sprint finish from the talented hold-up contingent.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If Diamonds Galore can dictate ideal positioning tracking Krak
scenarios.body: The Henderson-trained gelding gets first run on the leader while avoiding traffic problems that could befall the hold-up horses. His recent consistent form and prominent style perfectly suits sitting second throughout before striking decisively.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Completely
scenarios.trigger: If Krak goes too slow and gets swamped by multiple closers
scenarios.body: The lack of early pace results in a messy cavalry charge where the most unexposed horse with untapped potential can emerge. Itsinthename's limited experience over hurdles could mask significant improvement for the Scholfield stable.

watchPoints.text: Watch if Krak gets soft early fractions as he could steal the race from the front with minimal pressure
Monitor the early positioning of hold-up horses Fasol and Fromheretoeternity as traffic could be decisive
Observe Diamonds Galore's jumping rhythm as any mistakes could compromise his ideal tracking position
Check if Dog Fox shows ring rustiness after 173-day absence despite his proven course and distance form
Watch for market moves on Itsinthename given his unexposed profile and potential stable confidence

races.name: Bangor-On-Dee Grand Wynnstay Handicap Chase (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Calico
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with class advantage having won valuable handicaps, good ground suits and Harry Skelton booking suggests confidence despite 28-day break
runners_data.comment: Not seen to best effect on heavy ground last month; bagged two big prizes last autumn
runners_data.spotlight: Won valuable handicaps on good to soft ground at Cheltenham (2m) and Ascot (2m1f) last autumn; safely held in Grand Annual at Cheltenham Festival in March and not seen to best effect on heavy ground at Ayr last month but comes here on a workable mark and must be considered.

runners_data.name: Gabriel's Getaway
runners_data.note: Hold-up style faces tactical disadvantage in small field, jumping concerns persist and 77-day absence adds uncertainty despite 7lb drop in weights
runners_data.comment: Comes with risk but he's well handicapped and will be suited by a return to good ground
runners_data.spotlight: Always comes with risk, given his jumping often lacks fluency and that he apparently needs to be held up in rear, but he's effectively 7lb lower than when keeping on well for second in valuable Ascot handicap (2m1f, good) in November and will be suited by this return to forecast good ground; blinkered for last two runs; cheekpieces tried today.

runners_data.name: Grain d'Oudairies
runners_data.note: Prominent style suits the pace scenario but comes here off back of disappointing effort and lacks the class edge of main rivals

runners_data.name: Personal Ambition
runners_data.note: Natural leader will ensure strong early pace, blinkers back on and 66-day break could sharpen him but Grand National failure raises stamina doubts at this trip
runners_data.comment: Form of wide-margin novice win in February is tricky to evaluate; pulled up since
runners_data.spotlight: Won three-runner novice chase by 17l at Newbury (2m, soft; first-time blinkers) in February but that form is tricky to evaluate, and he was pulled up in the Grand Annual at Cheltenham in March; still needs to prove he can handle his current handicap mark and that he's fully effective on the forecast good ground.

runners_data.name: Homme Public
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse disadvantaged by likely pace shape, returning from wind surgery after 77-day break with poor recent form trend
runners_data.comment: Well below best last season but had wind op in March; too well handicapped to rule out
runners_data.spotlight: Well below best during five-race campaign last season and absent since pulled up on soft ground in February; had wind surgery the following month, though, and ought to be better suited by the forecast quicker conditions here; too well handicapped to rule out; swaps visor for refitted blinkers.

runners_data.name: Sir Tivo
runners_data.note: Prominent runner returning from long 213-day break but good ground specialist with excellent course record who thrives when fresh
runners_data.comment: Signed off with good-ground win in the autumn; may find younger rivals better handicapped
runners_data.spotlight: Good-ground specialist who made all in small field at Wetherby (1m7f, good) on latest outing in the autumn, his 11th chase success; won when fresh last spring but is slightly out of the weights here and may find younger rivals better handicapped.

runners_data.name: Obsessedwithyou
runners_data.note: Front-running mare in excellent form with 4-8 chase record, 5lb claimer reduces effective weight and good ground suits perfectly
runners_data.comment: Made all in three-runner mares' chase last month and is now 4-8 over fences
runners_data.spotlight: Made all in three-runner mares' chase at Wincanton (1m7f, good) last month and is now 4-8 over fences; faces tougher task from 3lb out of the weights here but is evidently in good nick, and new jockey Isabelle Ryder claims 5lb.

races.paceDynamic: Personal Ambition and Obsessedwithyou will dispute the early lead in this small field, with both confirmed front-runners likely to ensure a genuine gallop from the start. The relatively short field of seven means there's limited scope for tactical maneuvering, and with two eager leaders up front, the pace should be honest throughout. This setup creates a race where prominent runners like Calico, Grain d'Oudairies and Sir Tivo can track the leaders without getting too far back, while hold-up horses Gabriel's Getaway and Homme Public face the challenge of making up ground in a race that may not develop the strongest finish. The genuine early pace favors prominent racers and those with tactical speed over pure hold-up merchants.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Trackers Prevail
scenarios.trigger: If the two leaders Personal Ambition and Obsessedwithyou go too fast early and weaken
scenarios.body: The honest pace will suit those sitting in behind the leaders who can quicken when the front two falter. Class horses like Calico and the good-ground loving Sir Tivo can use their tactical speed to strike.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If one of the leaders gets first run on the other and kicks clear
scenarios.body: Obsessedwithyou's recent winning form and ability to make all could prove decisive if she can get the better of Personal Ambition early. Her tactical advantage from the front would be hard to peg back in this small field.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Charge Success
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is particularly strong and the field comes back to the closers
scenarios.body: Gabriel's Getaway and Homme Public could benefit if the front-runners go too hard and the race falls apart. Their hold-up style would then become an advantage as they pick up the pieces late.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Early
scenarios.trigger: If both leaders make jumping errors or one refuses to go on
scenarios.body: The race could become a sprint from halfway if the early pace setters exit or slow dramatically. This would create a tactical free-for-all where any style could prevail depending on position.

watchPoints.text: Personal Ambition and Obsessedwithyou could go too fast early if they get into a speed duel, compromising both their chances
Sir Tivo's 213-day absence is significant despite his fresh-running ability and needs watching for ring fitness
Gabriel's Getaway's jumping must improve significantly as his fluency issues become more costly in a race run at genuine pace
Homme Public returning from wind surgery with poor recent form needs to prove the operation was successful
Watch for how aggressively Obsessedwithyou's 5lb claimer rides the early pace as inexperience could disrupt tactics

races.name: Classic Additions Handicap Chase

runners_data.name: Cahier's Den
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with gently improving handicap form, but 46 days off and needs to find more at the business end
runners_data.comment: Improvement as a chaser continues gently, and went close at Newcastle latest; chance.
runners_data.spotlight: RPRs have been improving gently since sent handicap chasing, and a better jump at the last may have seen him oblige at Newcastle latest (3m, good to soft); won't mind good ground, having won an Irish point on it.

runners_data.name: Special John
runners_data.note: Strong prominent style but concerning as beaten favourite in last three starts, though Wincanton second suggests back on track
runners_data.comment: Beaten favourite on last three runs, but back on track last time out; remains of interest.
runners_data.spotlight: Beaten favourite on last three starts, albeit one upped to 3m4f and Class 3 and another over hurdles; largely back on track with last month's Wincanton second, and doesn't appear weighted out of further gains.

runners_data.name: Good Work
runners_data.note: Experienced prominent runner but surprisingly error-prone (1-37 record) and pulled up latest, frame chance at best
runners_data.comment: 1-37; another error-strewn round when fourth over C&D latest; still on a career-low mark.
runners_data.spotlight: 1-37 and still surprisingly error-prone despite so much chasing experience, leaving his mark on several fences en route to a 8l C&D fourth latest (good); frame finish probable but hard to predict better even off this career-low mark whilst the mistakes remain; cheekpieces return.

runners_data.name: Kenzo Des Bruyeres
runners_data.note: Natural front-runner with dual Irish point wins but tactics haven't worked in rules racing yet, wears cheekpieces
runners_data.comment: Dual 3m Irish point winner, making most; no surprise if taking a step forward now chasing.
runners_data.spotlight: Dual 3m Irish point winner (good to yielding, soft) making most; similar or same tactics haven't borne fruit in short rules career to date, but no surprise if he improves for fences as a half-brother to triple 3m chase scorer; may be worth chancing in a weak race.

runners_data.name: Slaney Opera
runners_data.note: Prefers sharp left-handers but found Fakenham fences coming too quickly last time, wears tongue strap and cheekpieces
runners_data.comment: Fakenham's sharp track coerced him into errors latest; can prove better than that again.
runners_data.spotlight: Majority of rules and point wins have been recorded around sharp left-handers, but found the fences coming too quickly even for him at Fakenham on last month's stable debut (3m5f, good; debuted cheekpieces retained here); no surprise were he to prove better than that again.

runners_data.name: On The Platform
runners_data.note: Last year's winner off 1lb higher but 562 days absent after pulling up, present form completely unknown
runners_data.comment: 1lb below the mark he defied in this race in 2024; pulled up on his sole run since.
runners_data.spotlight: Mastered Getaway Glory up the run-in to land this contest off 1lb higher in 2024 (good to soft); present attainment level a matter of conjecture, having pulled up on sole outing since.

runners_data.name: Walking The Walk
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist with poor conversion rate (2-27) but proven C&D performer, wears tongue strap after 364-day break
runners_data.comment: 2-27 over fences, and no wins since 2023; absent since beaten 47l in this last year.
runners_data.spotlight: Conversion rate of just 2-27 over fences; several long absences following his last win in summer 2023, and hasn't been since a 47l last of five finishers in this race last year; best watched.

runners_data.name: Gilbertina
runners_data.note: Prominent runner claiming 5lbs but heavy defeats disguised by respectable positions, wears tongue strap and trip may stretch stamina
runners_data.comment: Not without hope, but did jump left and didn't stay upped to 3m at Fakenham latest.
runners_data.spotlight: Claims on March's Newcastle third (2m4f, good to soft), but cosmetically respectable form figures this year disguise one or two heavy defeats, this trip as much the issue as her jumping left at Fakenham latest.

runners_data.name: Getaway Glory
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse placed twice at C&D including second in this race last year, but completely out of sorts in 2024
runners_data.comment: Close third to On The Platform in this race in 2024; out of sorts this year, however.
runners_data.spotlight: Placed on both previous C&D starts, including when beaten under 1l by On The Platform in this race (good to soft; headed last); out of sorts this year, however, and needs a positive response to wind surgery.

runners_data.name: Friends Don't Ask
runners_data.note: Prominent runner showing first form since summer with 80-1 Fontwell third, but 11-year-old consistency questionable
runners_data.comment: Fontwell third latest was first piece of form since summer 2024; needs to back it up.
runners_data.spotlight: First form since summer 2024 when an 80-1 third at Fontwell this month (3m2f, good); trip and ground as much to suit again this time, but no certainty to back up that effort.

races.paceDynamic: Kenzo Des Bruyeres will lead from the start with his proven front-running style, but faces immediate pressure from four prominent runners (Cahier's Den, Special John, Good Work, Slaney Opera) all wanting to track close. This congestion will create a searching gallop through the middle stages as they jostle for position approaching the business end. The sustained pace will set up perfectly for the hold-up horses Walking The Walk and Getaway Glory to deliver late challenges, making this a race that strongly favours patient tactics and finishing kick over early positioning.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Prevail
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent pack goes too hard chasing Kenzo Des Bruyeres through the middle stages
scenarios.body: The sustained gallop will empty the tanks of the early pace-setters, allowing the patient runners to sweep past in the final half-mile. Walking The Walk and Getaway Glory can use their proven C&D form to maximum advantage.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Kenzo Des Bruyeres gets an uncontested lead and dictates moderate fractions
scenarios.body: His dual Irish point wins show he has the stamina to sustain a long kick, and if the prominent horses fail to apply enough pressure early, he can have enough left to resist late challenges. James Bowen can judge the pace perfectly from the front.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Runners Strike
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent quartet can force a strong pace without emptying their own tanks
scenarios.body: Special John or Cahier's Den can use their recent form edge to break clear from the chasing pack before the hold-up horses get into gear. Their class advantage over the field becomes decisive in a truly-run race.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Favours Outsider
scenarios.trigger: If the pace battle becomes messy with multiple fallers or mistakes at crucial fences
scenarios.body: Friends Don't Ask can benefit from a muddling contest where his recent Fontwell third suggests he's found form again. The 80-1 winner profile could repeat if the fancied horses encounter trouble.

watchPoints.text: Kenzo Des Bruyeres must be allowed an uncontested lead early or his front-running tactics will backfire spectacularly
Special John needs to overcome his recent habit of failing as favourite, particularly with Matt Griffiths taking over riding duties
Good Work's jumping errors could cause carnage in the prominent pack where four horses will be tightly bunched
On The Platform's fitness after 562 days off will be revealed early, but his course winner's knowledge could be crucial
Walking The Walk's stamina reserves at age 11 after 364 days absent will determine if he can repeat his strong C&D record

races.name: Ladies Day On Saturday 23rd May Novices' Handicap Chase (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Park Annonciade
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who can track the pace and has winning form over fences, but the strong gallop may expose stamina doubts over this trip
runners_data.comment: Made most at Huntingdon last month (2m, good) and backed that up latest; rivals for lead.
runners_data.spotlight: Less contested lead than often the case when making it seventh time lucky over fences at Huntingdon last month (2m, good), and Stratford second off 6lb higher since consolidated that form; up another 1lb here but pace rivalry could prove more the issue.

runners_data.name: Is This For Real
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner under Liam Harrison who has won from the lead twice this year but faces fierce pace competition from two other leaders
runners_data.comment: Okay mark for chasing/handicap debut; not wholly wedded to recent assertive tactics.
runners_data.spotlight: 3-4 under Liam Harrison, gaining this year's Newcastle (good to soft) and Huntingdon (good) hurdles wins from the front but earlier bumper and point gains came under patient tactics; no chasers in immediate pedigree but his mark looks about right for this chasing/handicap debut.

runners_data.name: Ice In The Veins
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer for Harry Skelton who made all in hurdle wins but needs to settle better and benefit from the expected strong pace
runners_data.comment: Made all in two novice hurdles (2m, 2m3f); pace rivalry if returning to those tactics.
runners_data.spotlight: Made all for two good-ground novice hurdle wins last November (2m, 2m3f); lesser form this year likely more to do with a refusal to settle under restraint than the move to handicaps, but a return to previous tactics may put him in a pace battle with a few here; chasers in pedigree.

runners_data.name: Nibras Gold
runners_data.note: Front-running dual flat winner returning after 231 days off with superior class but may be vulnerable to fitness after the long layoff
runners_data.comment: Bountiful Flat/hurdles campaign last summer; two chasing seconds in 2024; goes well fresh.
runners_data.spotlight: Dual 1m4f Flat winner (made all) and Summer Hurdle third last year, and jumped perfectly well when second on two of three chase starts in summer 2024; record of 62121 when returning from breaks of over 200 days.

runners_data.name: Pigeon House
runners_data.note: Can do too much in front but won making all at Catterick in March, returns after 73 days off with trainer having poor recent form
runners_data.comment: Claiming hurdle win in March (1m7f, good); didn't last out on the Flat since; chase debut.
runners_data.spotlight: Can do too much in front but no alarms when making all in a Catterick claiming hurdle for Jennie Candlish in March (1m7f, good); out of a half-sister to a minor chase winner, but not bred for this job otherwise.

runners_data.name: King Ulanda
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who won off 4lb lower in autumn but has flopped twice since March and carries big fitness concerns
runners_data.comment: Another hurdles win last autumn (2m1f, good), but two flops and a fall more recently.
runners_data.spotlight: Productive autumn included a Carlisle hurdles win (2m1f, good) off 4lb lower; two flops either side of a late fall since March, however, and doesn't enter this chasing debut in the same good heart as some.

runners_data.name: Hudson
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who needs to prove he can translate hurdle form to fences and has been absent for 120 days
runners_data.comment: Trip to blame for backwards step last time; not an obvious one for chasing on pedigree.
runners_data.spotlight: Run of progressive hurdling RPRs halted by an unsuccessful step up to 2m7f back in January; not bred for fences and needs to prove able to translate his better work back to good ground, but trip more suitable again.

races.paceDynamic: Pigeon House, Is This For Real, and Nibras Gold will clash for the early lead, creating a fierce gallop from the start. All three are confirmed front-runners who struggle to settle, guaranteeing a strong pace throughout this 2m1½f test. The relentless gallop will stretch the field and expose any stamina limitations, particularly over Bangor's demanding circuit. This pace scenario strongly favours hold-up horses like Ice In The Veins who can pick up the pieces late when the pace-setters weaken.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Strong Pace Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If all three front-runners engage in a speed duel from the off
scenarios.body: The sustained gallop will drain Pigeon House, Is This For Real and Nibras Gold, setting up the race for closers who can stay the trip. Ice In The Veins and King Ulanda benefit most from their patient tactics when others stop.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pigeon House Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Pigeon House gets an uncontested lead while rivals track
scenarios.body: Charlie Todd can dictate fractions and save enough for a strong finish, replicating the Catterick win where he made all unopposed. The prominent runners Park Annonciade and Hudson can track and challenge late.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Nibras Gold Class
scenarios.trigger: If Nibras Gold's superior flat speed allows him to dominate the pace
scenarios.body: His dual flat winner's class and Summer Hurdle form gives him the tactical speed to control this field when fresh after 231 days off. Stan Sheppard can use his pace weapon to dictate terms throughout.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Tactical Meltdown
scenarios.trigger: If the front-runners go too fast early and none settle
scenarios.body: All three leaders will weaken dramatically in the final half-mile, creating chaos and allowing any horse with stamina reserves to sweep past. The entire complexion changes as tactical speed becomes irrelevant.

watchPoints.text: Pigeon House could steal the race if he gets an uncontested lead while his two pace rivals take each other on
Ice In The Veins must settle early for Harry Skelton or he'll get caught up in the pace battle despite his hold-up style
Nibras Gold's 231-day absence is a major fitness concern despite his superior class credentials
King Ulanda and Hudson both return from lengthy breaks and need to prove their fitness in a race likely to become a stamina test
The three confirmed front-runners will create early tempo but watch which one can sustain it longest up Bangor's demanding home straight
